To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RSK technique can switch faster and track delay variation across process corners.
RSK can improve the switching performance of dynamic gates by up to 1.9x compared to CONV for 20 legs and upto 32 legs compared to 20 legs for the CONV keeper.
the rate sensing keeper (RCK) is a novel technique for dynamic keeper design which can improve the speed of wide dynamic gates by 1.9x and scale up to 32 legs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new keeper circuit that can be used for wide OR structures.
the development of new techniques to improve the performance of dynamic logic circuits.
developing a robust keeper design that can scale to future technologies and improve the performance of dynamic logic gates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RSK is the best keeper technique to be used in dynamic logic circuits.
the proposed rate sensing keeper technique is the best alternative for wide dynamic logic structures.
RSK is the most promising keeper design technique for future technologies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an adaptive keeper design technique which is able to track the variation across the different process, supply, and temperature corners.
RSK is a promising technique to improve the performance of dynamic circuits for the future technology nodes.
RSK can be used for wide dynamic gates to improve the performance and can scale upto large number of legs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RSK design can be a viable alternative to the conventional feedback keeper for the wide dynamic logic gates.
the RSK can be used to design dynamic logic gates with a large number of inputs (upto 32) and can also be extended to other dynamic circuits such as dynamic flip-flops.
the rate sensing technique can be applied in a wide variety of logic circuits to achieve superior performance.
